story_type: burning fishing boat, two men in a life raft, cutter small boat pickup
hook: Their fishing boat was on fire. They were in a raft.
narration: Their fishing boat was burning ten miles off Washington, and the two men aboard were in a life raft.
The sixty foot Portlock had caught fire off Long Beach.
Before abandoning ship into the raft, they radioed their position to the Coast Guard.
A canister life raft inflates itself in seconds when its line is pulled, so a crew can get clear of a fire fast.
The Cutter Active arrived and launched a small boat crew to the raft.
They pulled both men out and brought them away from the fire.
Behind them, the empty Portlock kept burning.
outcome: Both men were rescued with no injuries, and the Cutter Active later sank the burning boat offshore.
title: Fishing boat on fire, two men in a raft
description:
On Aug. 31, 2009, the two crewmen of the 60-foot fishing vessel Portlock abandoned ship into a life raft when their boat caught fire about 10 miles off Long Beach, Washington. A small boat crew from the Coast Guard Cutter Active picked them up.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Kelly Parker, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/67539/coast-guard-responds-60-foot-vessel-fire
